examInfo.title: JAMB Economics Practice Questions
examInfo.subject: Economics
examInfo.instructions: Choose the correct option from A-D for each question.

questions.question: Economics is defined as the study of

options.B: Scarcity and choice

questions.explanation: Economics is fundamentally the study of how societies allocate scarce resources among unlimited wants, making it the study of scarcity and choice.

questions.question: The opportunity cost of a choice is

options.A: The money cost of the choice
options.B: The time spent making the choice
options.C: The value of the next best alternative forgone
options.D: The total cost of all alternatives

questions.explanation: Opportunity cost is the value of the next best alternative that must be given up when making a choice.

questions.question: When demand increases and supply remains constant, the price will

options.B: Increase

questions.explanation: When demand increases while supply remains constant, there is excess demand, which drives the price upward.

questions.question: The law of demand states that

options.A: As price increases, quantity demanded increases
options.B: As price decreases, quantity demanded decreases
options.C: As price increases, quantity demanded decreases
options.D: Price and quantity demanded are unrelated

questions.explanation: The law of demand states that there is an inverse relationship between price and quantity demanded, ceteris paribus.

questions.question: Elasticity of demand measures

options.A: The change in demand over time
options.B: The responsiveness of quantity demanded to price changes
options.C: The total demand for a product
options.D: The maximum price consumers will pay

questions.explanation: Price elasticity of demand measures how responsive quantity demanded is to changes in price.

questions.question: In perfect competition, firms are

options.B: Price takers

questions.explanation: In perfect competition, individual firms have no control over price and must accept the market price, making them price takers.

questions.question: Gross Domestic Product (GDP) measures

options.B: The total value of goods and services produced within a country
options.C: The total exports of a country

questions.explanation: GDP measures the total monetary value of all finished goods and services produced within a country's borders in a specific time period.

questions.question: Inflation is defined as

options.A: A decrease in the general price level
options.B: An increase in the general price level

questions.explanation: Inflation is a sustained increase in the general price level of goods and services in an economy over time.

questions.question: The central bank's main function is to

options.B: Control the money supply and monetary policy

questions.explanation: The central bank's primary function is to control the money supply and implement monetary policy to maintain economic stability.

questions.question: Unemployment that occurs due to changes in technology is called

options.B: Structural unemployment

questions.explanation: Structural unemployment occurs when there is a mismatch between workers' skills and job requirements, often due to technological changes.

questions.question: The production possibility curve shows

options.A: The relationship between price and quantity
options.B: The maximum combinations of goods that can be produced

questions.explanation: The production possibility curve (PPC) shows the maximum combinations of two goods that can be produced with available resources and technology.

questions.question: A monopoly is characterized by

options.B: Few sellers and many buyers

questions.explanation: A monopoly is a market structure with only one seller (producer) and many buyers, giving the seller significant market power.

questions.question: Fiscal policy involves

options.B: Government spending and taxation

questions.explanation: Fiscal policy refers to government's use of spending and taxation to influence the economy.

questions.question: The marginal utility of a good

options.B: Always decreases with consumption
options.D: May increase or decrease with consumption

questions.explanation: According to the law of diminishing marginal utility, the marginal utility of a good decreases as more units are consumed.

questions.question: Balance of payments records

options.B: All economic transactions between a country and the rest of the world

questions.explanation: Balance of payments is a comprehensive record of all economic transactions between residents of a country and the rest of the world.

questions.question: Economic growth is measured by

options.B: Increase in real GDP

questions.explanation: Economic growth is typically measured by the percentage increase in real GDP over time.

questions.question: The multiplier effect refers to

options.A: The effect of price changes on demand
options.B: The amplified impact of initial spending on total income
options.C: The effect of interest rates on investment
options.D: The impact of taxes on consumption

questions.explanation: The multiplier effect describes how an initial change in spending leads to a larger change in total income and output.

questions.question: Public goods are characterized by

options.B: Non-rivalry and non-excludability

questions.explanation: Public goods are non-rival (one person's consumption doesn't reduce availability to others) and non-excludable (difficult to prevent people from using them).

questions.question: The law of supply states that

options.A: As price increases, quantity supplied decreases
options.B: As price increases, quantity supplied increases
options.C: Price and quantity supplied are unrelated

questions.explanation: The law of supply states that there is a positive relationship between price and quantity supplied, ceteris paribus.

questions.question: Comparative advantage refers to

options.A: Producing everything more efficiently than others
options.B: Producing at the lowest opportunity cost

questions.explanation: Comparative advantage exists when a country can produce a good at a lower opportunity cost than other countries.

questions.question: Market failure occurs when

options.B: Markets fail to allocate resources efficiently

questions.explanation: Market failure occurs when the free market fails to allocate resources efficiently, often due to externalities, public goods, or market power.

questions.question: The Phillips curve shows the relationship between

options.B: Price and quantity

questions.explanation: The Phillips curve illustrates the inverse relationship between inflation and unemployment rates in the short run.

questions.question: Externalities are

options.A: Costs or benefits that affect only the producer
options.B: Costs or benefits that affect third parties

questions.explanation: Externalities are costs or benefits that affect parties who did not choose to incur those costs or benefits.

questions.question: The marginal propensity to consume (MPC) is

options.A: Total consumption divided by total income
options.B: Change in consumption divided by change in income
options.C: Total savings divided by total income
options.D: Change in savings divided by change in income

questions.explanation: MPC is the fraction of additional income that is spent on consumption, calculated as the change in consumption divided by the change in income.

questions.question: Devaluation of a currency means

options.B: The currency becomes weaker
options.D: The currency is removed from circulation

questions.explanation: Devaluation is a deliberate downward adjustment of a country's currency value relative to other currencies, making it weaker.
